_notes: B10 — Meal start and end, field (catalog B10, plan test-plans/journey-b/b10-meal-start-end.md, recording docs/media/journey-b/b10-meal-start-end.mp4, PET-12648 automation / WEBPET-1529 manual, runner row B10-001). Transport, not simulation, happy path only.

A meal punch is an ordinary Time In whose Job is the meal job (fixture.json mealJob 4203 — Amy's device shows it as '0 - LUNCH'). The master plan's UnpaidBreakCard guess is superseded by the recording, which shows the meal start and its return both landing as plain TimeCard/TI records, never on a break-card table: expected.envelope.absentTags names both break-card sections so a refactor that reintroduces them fails. The 30-minute minimum is enforced on the device only, before any record exists, so it is not automatable via XML.

Three records for one employee (6001): 07:15 clock-in on the work job 4201, 12:00 meal start on the meal job 4203, 12:35 return to the work job. Only the meal-return record carries a GPS fix, as the plan specifies (gpsFixes 1). jobOccurrences: the meal job appears once, the work job twice. No header punchTime — the old envelope passed none.
dayOffset -3: B10 owns day -3 — sharing an employee-day with a sibling under workers=2 would trip the office's duplicate-Time-In rule.

expected.intervals: the stored meal-return instant minus the stored meal-start instant is 35 minutes (2100000 ms). A real sync has the device stamp its own seconds; this envelope controls them exactly, so each stored instant equals the sent one verbatim (B10-R4).

expected.cards[2] (panel: true) is the meal-return row whose Time In panel the grid check opens — Phase must read the WORK job, the worker having been returned to it, not the lunch job; display names come from fixture.json. The grid check also asserts each row's Warning status and the 'Time-In has no closing punch' group (B3 proves two open Time-Ins for one employee render so). grid.absentIssueGroupPattern: no meal/lunch/break issue group may ever appear (B10-R7); the spec compiles it case-insensitively.
cleanup: the timeCards step sweeps 6001's fixture day before the import and deletes the imported cards after the test; the flow passes sweep:false so exactly one cleanup path is live.
